topic: Ollama v0.40.11: is it worth re-pulling your models?
thesis: Ollama v0.40.11's patch notes settle the question: updating swaps the app and never your pulled models, so the only downloads worth your evening are the new ones -- phonon at 113MB and the d3 decision models.
explanation_path: Establish what an update actually replaces before touching any feature: the Ollama application is one thing, and the models it pulled are files in a separate directory (~/.ollama/models and its siblings) that the updater does not write to. With that separation in place, read the v0.40.11 notes as a checklist of what changed in the app: speech generation on macOS, and the d3 decision-model family in four sizes. Then place .11 on the release calendar -- one calendar day after .10, two after .9 -- so the viewer can tell a routine bump from an urgent hotfix; the notes flag no breaking changes. The one counterexample that explains the re-download myth comes last: v0.40.2's background upgrades of pre-0.40 models, which kept the original on disk as a backup and only demanded a re-pull if you downgraded below 0.40. The payoff is the decision rule the viewer keeps: update the app always, re-pull never, pull new only when a feature names a model.

claims.claim: Ollama v0.40.11's headline change is speech generation on macOS: ollama run plays text or a chat model's reply aloud, and apps can stream audio through the OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech endpoint.
v0.40.11 also ships the d3 decision-model family from vLLM Semantic Router, sized 2B, 4B, 9B, and 27B, for classifying text, answering yes or no, and scoring options with probabilities.

v0.40.11 is a routine bump, not a hotfix: it was released 24 Oct 00:30, one calendar day after v0.40.10 (23 Oct 15:03) and two days after v0.40.9 (22 Oct 01:33), and none of those three release notes flag a breaking change.

An Ollama update replaces the application, not the models: pulled models live in ~/.ollama/models on macOS, /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models on Linux, and C:\Users\%username%\.ollama\models on Windows, directories the update mechanisms never write to.

The only model-touching change in the 0.40 line came in v0.40.2: models pulled with earlier versions were upgraded in the background on first run with the original kept on disk as a backup, and it is a downgrade below 0.40, not an update, that forces a re-pull.
Updating is one step per platform: macOS and Windows download updates automatically and apply them by clicking Restart to update in the taskbar or menubar, and Linux re-runs the install script.
The new speech capability costs one new pull, not a re-pull: phonon:latest downloads at 113MB, and the packages require Apple Silicon and Ollama 0.40.9 or later.
Trying the new decision models is an evening-sized pull measured in single digits: d3:2b downloads at 3.1GB - 3.2GB with a 256K context window, while the 27B sibling runs 29GB - 30GB.
The Windows docs confirm the app/model separation from the removal side: even the uninstaller leaves downloaded models alone when OLLAMA_MODELS was moved.

key_numbers.label: phonon:latest download size (the whole speech feature)

analogy_candidates.mapping: Updating Ollama is like updating the music player app on your phone -- the player changes, the songs on your storage do not, and re-downloading only enters the picture when you want a new album (phonon, d3).
analogy_candidates.limit: Models are not inert songs; they are format-coupled to the engine, and the v0.40.2 runner swap shows a player update can rewrite your library's format under you -- with a backup kept, but disk usage temporarily doubled.

misconceptions.myth: Every Ollama update re-downloads your models.
misconceptions.reality: The updater replaces the app while pulled models sit untouched in ~/.ollama/models, and the 0.40 line's only model change (v0.40.2) was an automatic background upgrade that kept the original as a backup (claims 4 and 5).

misconceptions.myth: v0.40.11 is an urgent hotfix you must drop everything for.
misconceptions.reality: It shipped one calendar day after v0.40.10 as a routine feature bump -- speech plus d3 -- with no breaking changes flagged in the notes (claim 3).

glossary.definition: An app that downloads and runs open AI models locally on your own machine.
Downloading a model from ollama.com's library onto your disk; the only large download in Ollama.
A model that turns written text into spoken audio, streamed as it generates.
A small model trained to classify input, answer yes or no, or score options instead of chatting.

unverified: How widespread the belief that updates re-download models actually is: the Reddit and forum threads surfaced by search could not be fetched this session (403), so the myth's reach is unmeasured.
No first-party or benchmark performance numbers exist for v0.40.11; any tokens-per-second or load-time claim must wait for a measurement on our own hardware.
When speech generation reaches Windows and Linux is not stated in the v0.40.11 notes, which say on macOS only.
suggested_outline:
Cold open on the two-line test: v0.40.11 shipped speech on macOS and the d3 decision models -- and its notes say nothing about the models you already have, which is exactly the point.
The mechanism that kills the myth: the updater swaps the app while models live in ~/.ollama, and the one time Ollama did touch models (v0.40.2) it upgraded them in the background with backups kept.
The rule and the one pull worth making: update always, re-pull never, pull new only when a feature names a model -- phonon at 113MB for speech, d3 at 3.1GB - 3.2GB for decisions.
notes:
GitHub prints release times in the viewer's timezone: the v0.40.11 page shows 24 Oct 00:30 while the tag's source assets carry the ISO stamp 2026-10-23T23:15:08Z; the page-printed date is the one quoted verbatim. The docs.ollama.com/install URL is a 404; the per-platform pages (/linux, /macos, /windows, /docker, /faq) are the live install-and-update pages. Thin spots: no official page states outright that updates leave models untouched -- claim 4 is assembled from the documented storage locations plus what each update mechanism replaces -- and the community threads behind the re-download myth returned 403, so the misconception is grounded in Ollama's own v0.40.2 note rather than community measurement. The Linux docs corroborate claim 6 (Update Ollama by running the install script again) and the speech docs corroborate claim 7 (Start Ollama v0.40.9 or later, then download Phonon).
- 03 checkpoint (unattended): angle confirmed -- the v0.40.11 patch notes decide whether re-pulling your models is worth the evening; slug unchanged.
- 03 rationale: classic band, one fact one consequence; the viewer already runs Ollama, so the brief targets the update-or-re-pull decision, not an install walkthrough.
viewer_situation: You've got Ollama 0.40-point-something on your gaming PC or Mac with a few models already pulled, and every update ping makes you wonder whether tonight is the night you re-download a hundred gigabytes.
process_steps: check the release notes for the version you are on, at github.com/ollama/ollama/releases
apply the update: click Restart to update on macOS or Windows, or re-run curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh on Linux (Docker: pull the ollama/ollama image again)
run ollama list to confirm every pulled model is still there, untouched
pull only what the notes actually add, e.g. ollama pull phonon for speech or ollama run d3 for decision models
re-pull an existing model only if you downgraded below 0.40 or deleted it, never because the app updated
objection: Absence of a warning is not a guarantee: Ollama has already changed model formats under users once with the v0.40.2 background upgrade, so your models are safe holds only until the next runner swap.
